# ezghcloud_hosted_queue_kafka_topic (Resource)

A topic on a Kafka cluster. Destroying it deletes this topic and its messages, nothing else; topics apps create are never touched unless imported.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster (hqc_) it is in. Changing it replaces the object.
- `name` (String) The topic's name. Changing it replaces the object.
- `project_id` (String) Project of the cluster. Changing it replaces the object.

### Optional

- `config` (Map of String) Topic settings as Kafka's strings: retention.ms, retention.bytes, cleanup.policy, min.insync.replicas, max.message.bytes, compression.type, segment.bytes. Only configured keys are read back; removing one returns it to the cluster's default.
- `partitions` (Number) Partitions, 1 to 1000 (the cluster's default_partitions when left out). Grows in place; fewer is refused at plan.
- `replication_factor` (Number) Copies of each partition, 1 to 3. Left out, the cluster's default, and three once the cluster grows to replicated. Raised in place; lowering it is refused at plan.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) cluster_id/name, with the vhost before the name for a RabbitMQ object.
- `organization_id` (String) Organization managed by the configured provider.
- `origin` (String) api if it was made through EZGH, broker if an app made it first (an imported object).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_hosted_queue_kafka_topic.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/CLUSTER_ID/NAME'
```
